summary: Pursue cannot be reached: the high case's year-5 value is 3.57 times the base case's, over the 2.5 limit, so no buy line or zone is published, and no claim clears that. The code's total is 61.65 against 70 (maximum reachable 65.15). The 10-K's single-supplier disclosure costs 15 moat points. Valuation decides how near the total gets: it scores 0 on a 7.46% base-case return, after -20 for rare growth and -10 for the low case. Core claim C1: the mature operating margin is at least Micron's own ten-year median of 27.645%, not the 17.98% industry median the code fades it to. If C1 is supported, the code's base case returns 14.05% a year with a buy line of $755.67, above the $690 price, and the total is 66.15. C2 rebuts the severe peak-earnings flag (TTM operating income at or above $99.34bn through FY2028). C3 says the code overcharges reinvestment. Both macro conditions hold today (US 10-year 4.867% below 5.5; CMDI_IG 0.25 below 0.5).
thesis_in_three_sentences: At $690 the market pays 7.45 times TTM EBIT, below Micron's own 25th percentile of 10.23, because it prices FY2026's 74.59% operating margin as a peak that will fall back to industry levels. Take-or-pay contracts with price floors, $134bn of them at minimum pricing, make Micron's own ten-year median margin of 27.645% the right end point rather than the 17.98% industry median (C1); on that margin the code's base case returns 14.05% a year. The case is wrong if TTM operating margin falls below 46.28% or TTM operating income below $85bn at two consecutive quarter-ends before the August 2028 quarter.

mispricing.market_view: On the code's Track B rule (margin fading from 74.59% to the 17.98% industry median over ten years), the $690 price needs 17.22% revenue growth a year for ten years, which at most 5% of 1,375 comparables achieved. If today's margin were simply held, it needs revenue to shrink 4.16% a year. Enterprise value is 7.45 times TTM EBIT, against an own median of 14.13 and a minimum of 6.19. The market is pricing a margin collapse, not a growth path.
mispricing.our_view: The fade's end point is too low for the business Micron has become. Its own ten-year median operating margin of 27.645%, a span that includes the FY2023 trough, is the better base rate, and the contracts signed in FY2026 put a floor under part of the volume (C1). FY2026 is not the earnings peak: the August 2026 quarter alone earned $43.75bn of operating income (C2). Cash generation is far above the code's free cash flow to the firm (C3). On C1 alone, the code's base case returns 14.05% a year and the buy line rises to $755.67.

catalyst.event: The FY2027 results and 10-K (fiscal year to early September 2027; the FY2026 release came on 30 Sep 2026) and the first-quarter FY2028 results. This is the first full fiscal year under the strategic customer agreements and the first period in which the Idaho fab's first wafers (mid-2027) add supply. TTM operating margin at or above 50% through those results would show that the fade the price assumes is not happening (C1).

supply_chain_position: The map places Micron in the memory-and-storage tier with high AI-capex exposure: about 60% of FY2026 revenue was data centre. Nvidia's and Qualcomm's 10-Ks name Micron as a memory supplier. Lam Research, Rambus and Silicon Motion name it as a customer. The 10-K names Samsung, SK hynix, Sandisk, CXMT and YMTC as competitors. The map proposes no chokepoint and the dossier records none, so the moat score gets no chokepoint points. The tier is not crowded; XSD had a 4-week outflow of 7.76% of assets and XLK an inflow of 1.38%.
valuation_reading: The code's base case takes consensus growth of 54.88% a year for two years, then base rates, with the margin fading to 17.98% (46.28% in year 5). Its exit is the DCF cap of 4.54 times EBIT, against 32.26 for the industry. That gives 7.46% a year (46.45% at the industry exit), a DCF value of $728.75 and a buy line of $560.94 against the $690 price. The low case returns -20.92% and the high case 38.63%; the high case is 3.57 times the base at year 5, so no zone is published. C1's what-if (margin_target 27.645%, priced after the claims were pushed) gives an exit of 6.25 times, 14.05% a year, a DCF value of $968.33 and a buy line of $755.67, a measured share of the gap of 1.0. The thesis makes no exit-multiple claim: the own EV/EBIT history covers 15 quarter-ends from November 2021 (median 14.13, 25th percentile 10.23, 75th 18.85), and its 85.51 maximum was set on trough earnings. The Analyst's caveats (overstated reinvestment, a 21.04% tax rate, net cash leaving out $30.0bn of long-term investments) all point to a higher value.
bull_case: Operating income was $43.75bn in the August 2026 quarter, at an 80.68% margin. Remaining performance obligations under take-or-pay agreements are $134bn, measured at minimum pricing, and are backed by $12.75bn of deposits and $7bn of letters of credit. Net cash on the broad basis is about $68.3bn. Consensus revenue rises to $319.7bn in FY2028. At 7.45 times TTM EBIT, the earnings yield stays high even if the margin halves, and the code's own base case returns 14.05% if the margin settles at Micron's own median.
bear_case: FY2026 was price, not volume: DRAM prices rose about 180% on bit growth in the mid-20% range. Operating margins over ten years ran from -36.97% to 74.59%, and revenue fell in 7 of 19 years, including -49.48% in FY2023. Micron, Samsung, SK hynix and CXMT are all adding capacity, and Micron guides about $25bn of capex in the first half of FY2027 alone. The agreements are estimated at only over 35% of revenue, and a Taiwan labour dispute affects about 60% of DRAM output. Insiders sold $338.53m and bought $7.82m.

peers.name: Samsung Electronics
peers.comparison: The largest memory maker and a named competitor. The dossier cites Counterpoint (via a secondary source) for Samsung's HBM revenue share rising from 21% to 33% between Q1 and Q2 2026, against Micron's 18%.

peers.name: SK hynix
peers.comparison: A named competitor and HBM leader, with a 50% HBM revenue share in Q2 2026 (Counterpoint, secondary). The cache holds no SK hynix figures.

peers.name: Sandisk
peers.comparison: A NAND competitor, deep-dived in this run, that has signed similar multi-year agreements with floor prices. Unlike Micron it has no DRAM and no fabs of its own.

peers.name: CXMT
peers.comparison: State-backed Chinese DRAM maker named in the 10-K, about 10% of DRAM revenue (Counterpoint, per industry reports). The main new supply risk to C1 and C2.

single_source_supplier.note: 10-K Note 21: Micron generally has multiple sources, but in some cases materials or production equipment are provided by a single supplier (Item 1 and 1A repeat it for materials, components and services). Read as single-source, as for KLIC in this run

largest_customer_share.note: Upper bound: 10-K Note 21 says no customer accounted for 10% or more of FY2026 revenue (one was 17% in FY2025); the true share is below 10%, under the 20% that costs moat points

kill_criteria.criterion: TTM operating margin below 46.28%, the code's year-5 base margin, at two consecutive quarter-ends before the August 2028 quarter. That is below the FY2018 peak of 49.34%, and would mean the price-band contracts have not changed the cycle.

TTM operating income below $85bn at two consecutive quarter-ends, meaning quarterly operating income averaging under about $21bn against $43.75bn in the August 2026 quarter. FY2026 would then have been the peak.
TTM operating cash flow less capex below $26.49bn, the code's year-1 free cash flow to the firm, at two consecutive quarter-ends. The code's reinvestment charge would then be right.

reopen_conditions: A later valuation run in which the high case's year-5 value is at most 2.5 times the base case's, so a buy line and zone are published. This is the blocker no claim can clear today.
The price at or below the code's base-case buy line of $560.94, or at or below $755.67 if the Judge supports C1.
TTM operating margin at or above 50% and TTM operating income above $99.34bn at the August 2027 quarter, the first full fiscal year under the strategic customer agreements (C1 and C2 holding).
The FY2026 proxy, when filed, showing executive pay tied to per-share or return metrics, plus a guidance record in the cache. Those inputs are worth up to 3.5 points of total, and are null today.
gaps: Guidance record: no history of guided against actual results is in the cache, so the guidance input is null (0 points).
Pay: the FY2026 proxy is not filed and no proxy rows are in the cache; CEO pay comes only from a secondary summary of the FY2025 proxy, so pay_tied_to_returns is null (0 points).

Remaining performance obligations ($134bn) and the strategic agreements' share of revenue (over 35%, secondary) are not cache series, so no claim uses them as a metric_ref; C1 and C2 test their effect through TTM margin and operating income.
HBM shares and CXMT's DRAM share come from secondary pages relaying Counterpoint; the November-quarter guidance comes from CNBC's report, not the release.

The 10-K's floor-price gross margin statement compares with 'peak quarterly margins in any past cycle'; the cache's quarterly history starts in November 2023, so FY2018's annual gross margin of 58.87% is used as a lower bound on that peak.
deviations: Pursue is blocked, so every section except the claims, kill criteria and reopen conditions is kept to a few sentences (step 2 of the instructions).
